title: HEARTLAND Protocol App — Clinical Implementation Companion for Rural Heart Failure
description: HEARTLAND Protocol App is an inspectable clinical implementation companion for rural and resource-limited heart failure workflows. Version 1.10.1 clarifies that resource tiers govern delivery capacity, not lower clinical goals, delayed indicated follow-up or exclusion from pharmacy and financial-assistance support. It separates trained recognition and escalation, qualified assessment, authorized decisions, referral contexts and accepted-transfer responsibility. A public four-step local-readiness guide and downloadable pack provide 12 synthetic scenarios, role/coverage worksheets, paper records and respectful-escalation expectations. Historical quality percentages are planning examples, not validated benchmarks or individualized care targets. The release retains recoverable examination, laboratory and education workflows, versioned provenance, organization-scoped ownership, professional review/contact documentation and queued notification-intent controls. The synthetic sandbox retains bilingual bounded language assistance, simulated outreach, read-only Copilot, population replay, SBAR drafts, Evidence Flow, Decision Receipts and 58 recording-specific authorized synthetic clips. Numerical risk, dose, referral and alert rules, database permissions and audio assets are unchanged. Scheduled recovery and external notification transport remain disabled. Preparing a resource, saving a record, accepting a notification or playing audio does not establish staff competence, patient contact, delivered care, clinical validation, institutional adoption, regulatory status, efficacy or patient outcomes. Real PHI and unsupervised patient use are outside this release.
notes: Release boundary: synthetic technical demonstration and controlled evaluation only. Verification includes typecheck, lint, unit/integration tests, production build, recording-specific release checks and desktop/mobile browser tests; skipped/TODO cases are not clinical validation. The 58-file audio release remains unchanged, with 28 current generation receipts and 30 historical unreceipted recordings; automated ASR/decoder checks are not human-listening certification. Earlier clinical script acceptance was reported by the project owner, not supplied as a direct signed attestation. Separate ambulatory entry, patient studies and institution-specific governance, staffing, coverage, privacy, security, accessibility and operational verification remain required. The HEARTLAND Risk Stratification Framework remains proposed and unvalidated against clinical outcomes.
